Target = official Ubuntu 24.04.5 WSL image with a task-created uid-1000 default user (same uid as the controller user) instead of the image OOBE user; a root-default target and other distributions were not measured.

The controller is the owner's existing (not disposable) distribution; only client-side actions ran there. wsl.exe -l -v before and after the task compare equal (diff exit 0); the target was unregistered (exit 0).

Exposure rows [O] (r1): private path not visible from the controller; abstract namespace, /mnt/wsl socket (0600, same uid) and loopback TCP reachable from the controller; loopback TCP reachable from Windows (nat); the controller used the target endpoint through `wsl.exe -d hm-g03b-732254 -u hg03t`; the private-path socket file is visible to Windows through \\wsl.localhost (Test-Path True). A Windows-side connection to that socket and abstract//mnt/wsl reachability from Windows were not measured.

Interpretation [I]: the private path holds only against plain filesystem access from another distribution; abstract, /mnt/wsl and loopback TCP placements are reachable by same-uid processes of other distributions, and wsl.exe gives any same-user process the target's endpoint (documented non-boundary). This is evidence for rejecting B4 and for the R-SE-03 'same-user convenience' label, not a failure trigger (sec. 5: only a reachable private path triggers placement redesign).
